_comment: Go<->Python parity matrix for splitting a fenced ```yaml block into the
files it documents. Two gates read docs/**/*.md and BOTH must cut the
They are two independent hand-written implementations of one rule, over one
corpus. That is the shape this repo keeps getting burned by, so neither
side asserts the other: both assert THIS table, which makes their agreement
Deliberately a CASE MATRIX, not a snapshot of the live docs tree. A snapshot
keyed by line number would need regenerating on every documentation edit -
churn that teaches people to regenerate without reading. These cases encode
the RULE, so they only change when the rule does.
`offsets` are 0-based line offsets, relative to the first line INSIDE the
fence, at which each segment starts. Callers add the fence's own line + 1 to
turn an offset into a reportable file line.

cases.name: no header - the whole block is one file
cases.why: The common case. A block with no file-header comment documents exactly one file.

cases.name: two files introduced by header comments
cases.why: The inheritance illustrations. Judged whole this is not even valid YAML (repeated top-level key), which says nothing about whether the documented config is right.

cases.name: three files
cases.why: federation-integration.md stacks a platform file and two tenant files.

cases.name: indented comment is prose, NOT a file boundary
cases.why: LOAD-BEARING. The header regex is anchored at column 0. With a leading \s* this indented comment (real, in for-domain-experts.md) would sever the block mid-mapping: the tail gets validated as its own document and the head silently loses the entries below it.

cases.name: trailing comment on a data line is not a header
cases.why: The regex must match the START of the line, so a filename mentioned in a trailing comment cannot be mistaken for a file boundary.

cases.name: comment without a yaml filename is not a header
cases.why: Only a comment naming a .yaml/.yml file starts a new documented file. Prose headings inside a block are ordinary comments.

cases.name: leading header at offset 0 does not produce an empty first segment
cases.why: A header on the very first line opens the first segment rather than closing an empty one.

cases.name: .yml spelling is a header too
cases.why: Both spellings appear in docs/; the regex uses .ya?ml.

cases.name: text before the first header stays with it
cases.why: Content preceding the first header is its own segment (an unnamed file), not discarded.
